functional_requirements_ahb.text: All bus transfers are timed by the rising edge of HCLK; the bus has a single clock-edge operation.
The bus reset signal HRESETn is active-LOW; it resets the system and the bus. It is the only active-LOW signal in AHB.
Each AHB transfer consists of two phases: an Address phase (one HCLK cycle unless extended by the previous data phase) and a Data phase (one or more HCLK cycles for the data, controlled by HREADY).

The address phase of any transfer occurs during the data phase of the previous transfer; address and data are pipelined to enable high-performance operation while leaving time for the Subordinate to respond.
HREADY HIGH at a rising edge of HCLK indicates the current transfer is complete; HREADY LOW inserts wait states (extends the data phase).
Each Subordinate drives its own HREADYOUT signal; the interconnect (multiplexor) combines all HREADYOUTs to produce the single HREADY broadcast to the Manager and all Subordinates.
An address decoder generates one HSELx per Subordinate. A Subordinate must sample HSELx, HADDR, and all control signals only when HREADY is HIGH (transfer completing).
Managers must not attempt to start an incrementing burst that crosses a 1KB address boundary. The minimum slave address allocation is 1KB so a burst cannot cross a decode boundary.
Subordinates must always provide a zero-wait-state OKAY response to IDLE transfers and must ignore the transfer.

Subordinates must always provide a zero-wait-state OKAY response to BUSY transfers and must ignore the transfer. BUSY may only be used in the middle of a burst, never to terminate a fixed-length burst.

HWRITE indicates direction: HIGH = write transfer (Manager drives HWDATA), LOW = read transfer (Subordinate drives HRDATA). HWRITE has the same timing as the address signals and must remain constant throughout a burst.
HSIZE, HBURST and the other control signals must remain constant throughout a burst transfer.
All transfers in a burst must be aligned to the address boundary equal to the size of the transfer (word transfers must align to HADDR[1:0]=2'b00; halfword transfers must align to HADDR[0]=1'b0).
Wrapping bursts (WRAP4/WRAP8/WRAP16) wrap when crossing an address boundary equal to the product of the number of beats and the transfer size; HSIZE and HBURST jointly determine the wrap boundary.
AHB ERROR response is a two-cycle response on HRESP: first cycle HRESP=1 with HREADY=0, second cycle HRESP=1 with HREADY=1. The Manager observes the ERROR on the second cycle.
Managers must not end a fixed-length burst (INCR4/8/16 or WRAP4/8/16) with a BUSY transfer; fixed-length bursts must terminate with a SEQ transfer.
Bursts may be terminated by a Subordinate ERROR response (Manager may cancel remaining transfers, must drive HTRANS=IDLE during the two-cycle ERROR) or by a multi-layer interconnect.

When Subordinate is requesting wait states (HREADY=0), the Manager must not change the transfer type, except for the limited cases: IDLE→NONSEQ, BUSY→SEQ (fixed-length burst), or BUSY→any other type (undefined-length burst when HREADY LOW).
When Subordinate is requesting wait states (HREADY=0), the Manager can only change the address once — during an IDLE transfer or after an ERROR response.

If the Manager requires locked accesses, it asserts HMASTLOCK. The bus is locked after a cycle with HMASTLOCK=1, HSEL=1, HREADY=1; unlocked after a cycle with HMASTLOCK=0, HREADY=1. All transfers in a locked sequence must be to the same Subordinate address region.

HPROT[3:0] (Issue A) or HPROT[6:0] (with Extended_Memory_Types property) provides protection control information about the access (Opcode/Data, User/Privileged, Bufferable/Modifiable/Cacheable, Allocate/Shareable). HPROT must remain constant throughout a burst.
If AHB5 Secure_Transfers property is True, HNONSEC indicates Non-secure (HIGH) vs Secure (LOW) transfer. HNONSEC is an address-phase signal and must be constant throughout a burst.

If AHB5 Exclusive_Transfers property is True, HEXCL marks a transfer as part of an Exclusive Access sequence; HMASTER carries a unique Manager identifier and HEXOKAY is returned by the Subordinate (drives the Exclusive Access Monitor).

If Write_Strobes property is True (Issue C addition), HWSTRB enables sparse writes — one strobe per byte lane of HWDATA; HWSTRB[n] corresponds to HWDATA[(8n+7):8n]. HWSTRB is a data-phase signal with the same validity rules as HWDATA.

functional_requirements_apb.text: All transfers on the APB are timed by the rising edge of PCLK.
The APB reset signal PRESETn is active-LOW and is normally connected directly to the system bus reset signal.
Every APB transfer has at least two PCLK cycles: a Setup phase (PSELx=1, PENABLE=0) followed by an Access phase (PSELx=1, PENABLE=1).
IDLE is the default state of the APB: PSELx=0, PENABLE=0.

When a transfer is required, the bus enters SETUP, asserting PSELx for the addressed Subordinate. The bus only remains in SETUP for one PCLK cycle and always moves to ACCESS on the next rising edge of PCLK.

PENABLE is asserted in ACCESS. PADDR, PWRITE, PSELx, and (for writes) PWDATA must remain stable across the SETUP→ACCESS transition. Exit from ACCESS is controlled by PREADY: PREADY=0 keeps the bus in ACCESS; PREADY=1 exits to IDLE (no further transfer) or to SETUP (immediately back-to-back transfer).
While PREADY remains LOW during an ACCESS phase, the following signals must remain unchanged: PADDR, PWRITE, PSELx, PENABLE, PWDATA, PSTRB, PPROT.
Peripherals that have a fixed two-cycle access can tie PREADY HIGH; PREADY can take any value when PENABLE is LOW.
Only one PSELx is asserted at a time (selecting exactly one Subordinate per transfer).
PSTRB write strobes must not be active during a read transfer (the bus master must drive all bits of PSTRB LOW for reads).
There is one PSTRB strobe per 8 bits of write data: PSTRB[n] corresponds to PWDATA[(8n+7):8n].
PSLVERR is only considered valid during the last cycle of an APB transfer, when PSEL, PENABLE, and PREADY are all HIGH. PSLVERR is recommended to be driven LOW outside this window.
APB peripherals are not required to support the PSLVERR pin. Where a peripheral does not include this pin, the appropriate input to the APB bridge is tied LOW.

A transaction that receives a PSLVERR error response might or might not have changed the state of the peripheral — implementation-specific. Read transactions that receive an error can return invalid data (no requirement to drive zero).

PPROT[2:0] (APB4) provides protection: [0] 0=normal/1=privileged; [1] 0=secure/1=nonsecure (HIGH-for-Non-secure); [2] 0=data/1=instruction. PPROT must remain constant when PREADY is LOW (wait states).
The APB protocol is not pipelined; use it to connect to low-bandwidth peripherals that do not require AXI/AHB performance.

error_response_conditions: AHB: Subordinate gives ERROR response (HRESP=1 over two cycles) for unsupported transfer / invalid access. Manager may cancel remaining burst transfers but must drive HTRANS=IDLE during the two-cycle ERROR.
APB: Subordinate may drive PSLVERR=1 in the last cycle of a transfer (PSEL=PENABLE=PREADY=1) to indicate failure. Peripheral state after error is implementation-specific.
AHB Exclusive (AHB5): HEXOKAY response is driven LOW if exclusive write failed (another Manager wrote in between).

protocol_overview.ahb_role: High-performance pipelined synchronous bus, single rising-edge HCLK. Single-Manager (AHB-Lite) by default; multi-Manager supported via an interconnect that provides arbitration.
protocol_overview.apb_role: Low-cost peripheral bus, not pipelined, two PCLK cycles minimum per transfer.
protocol_overview.bridging: An AHB-to-APB bridge appears as a Subordinate on the AHB side and a Manager on the APB side, performing rate adaptation.

atomicity.ahb_lite: HMASTLOCK locked sequence; AHB5 adds Exclusive transfers via HEXCL / HEXOKAY

evidence.quote: The Manager starts a transfer by driving the address and control signals. ... Every transfer consists of: Address phase — One address and control cycle. Data phase — One or more cycles for the data. ... A Subordinate cannot request that the address phase is extended ... a Subordinate can request that the Manager extends the data phase by using HREADY.

HTRANS[1:0]: 0b00 IDLE (no data transfer; Subordinate must give zero wait state OKAY); 0b01 BUSY (Manager continuing a burst but cannot complete next transfer immediately); 0b10 NONSEQ (single transfer or first transfer of a burst); 0b11 SEQ (remaining transfers in a burst, address related to previous).

If the Manager requires locked accesses, then it must also assert the HMASTLOCK signal. This signal indicates to any Subordinate that the current transfer sequence is indivisible. ... The bus is locked after a cycle with HMASTLOCK asserted, HSEL asserted if present, and HREADY is HIGH.
Managers must not attempt to start an incrementing burst that crosses a 1KB address boundary. All transfers in a burst must be aligned to the address boundary equal to the size of the transfer.

Subordinates use HREADYOUT to insert wait states. ... When the Subordinate is requesting wait states, the Manager must not change the transfer type, except as described in: IDLE transfer; BUSY transfer fixed-length burst; BUSY transfer undefined length burst. ... When the Subordinate is requesting wait states, the Manager can only change the address once — during an IDLE transfer or after an ERROR response.
The Subordinate uses HRESP to indicate the success or failure of a transfer. ... ERROR is a two-cycle response.

The APB protocol is not pipelined, use it to connect to low-bandwidth peripherals that do not require the high performance of the AXI protocol. The APB protocol relates a signal transition to the rising edge of the clock, to simplify the integration of APB peripherals into any design flow. Every transfer takes at least two cycles.

At T1, a write transfer starts with address PADDR, write data PWDATA, write signal PWRITE, and select signal PSEL, being registered at the rising edge of PCLK. This is called the Setup phase of the write transfer. At T2, enable signal PENABLE, and ready signal PREADY, are registered at the rising edge of PCLK.
You can use PSLVERR to indicate an error condition on an APB transfer. ... PSLVERR is only considered valid during the last cycle of an APB transfer, when PSEL, PENABLE, and PREADY are all HIGH.
IDLE PSELx=0 PENABLE=0 (default state). SETUP PSELx=1 PENABLE=0 (transfer required). ACCESS PSELx=1 PENABLE=1 (waits while PREADY=0).
